faq.q: Where do I put my finger?
faq.a: Put it just under the first word of the line, not on top, so you can still see the letters.
Your finger gives your eyes something to follow. It helps you keep your place and stops you skipping words or lines.

faq.q: How do I use a ruler to read?
faq.a: Lay the ruler under the line you are reading and move it down one line at a time. A strip of card or a bookmark works too.

faq.q: What do I do at a full stop?
faq.a: A full stop means the sentence is over. Take a little breath, then start the next sentence.
asks: What does a full stop mean?

faq.q: Is it babyish to use my finger?
faq.a: Not at all! Lots of grown-ups run a finger or a pen along the line when they read something important. Use any tool that helps you.

facts: A reading ruler or a strip of card can cover the lines below, so only one line shows at a time.
Pointing under words is a common way to help readers keep their place.

quiz.say: Where should your finger go when you read?
quiz.why: Under the word, so your finger guides your eyes but does not hide the letters.

wrong.1: On top, your finger would hide the letters.
wrong.2: Your finger stays on the line you are reading now.

quiz.say: What do you do at the end of a line?
quiz.show: At the end of a line…

options.show: Slide down to the next line
options.say: Slide down to the next line

quiz.why: Slide down one line and go back to the left, where the next line starts.

wrong.1: No need to stop. Just slide down to the next line.
wrong.2: Going to the top would make you read the same lines again.
